title: Sekar's diary: the batik workshop
text:
Tuesday 12 March, evening

Today our class visited a batik workshop in Pekalongan, and my fingers are still tingling. I am going to write everything down tonight while I remember it.

We arrived at nine o'clock. Our guide, Ibu Lestari, has been making batik for thirty years, and she has hands that move so quickly that I could hardly follow them. She showed us a long strip of white cotton pinned to a wooden frame. "Before any colour goes on," she said, "the cloth must be protected." Then she lifted a little copper tool with a thin spout, called a canting, and dipped it into a pot of melted wax. Slowly, steadily, she drew flowers and curling leaves across the cloth.

I thought the wax was only decoration, but it is much cleverer than that. The wax blocks the dye, so anywhere it has been drawn stays white when the cloth is dipped into the colour. After the first dye dries, the maker covers new parts with wax and dips the cloth again. Each layer of colour takes another round of drawing and dyeing, so a really detailed piece can take weeks.

Then we all had a go. I was given a small square of cloth and my own canting. I will admit that my first line wobbled like a worm, and I got a blob of wax on my thumb. Dewi laughed at me, then spilt a whole spoonful of it on her sleeve, so I stopped feeling embarrassed. By the end my leaf looked like a leaf, even if it was a bit lopsided.

The last step surprised me most. The finished cloth is boiled in hot water, and the wax melts away, leaving the pattern clear against the background. Ibu Lestari held up a sarong she had finished that morning. Its blue and brown waves looked as if they were moving.

On the bus home, Wulan counted how many different batik patterns she could spot on people's clothes in the streets. She reached eleven before we gave up. I feel I will never look at a batik shirt in the same way again, because now I know how many hours of patience are woven into it.

Tomorrow I am going to show Mum my wobbly leaf. She will say it is the most beautiful one she has seen.
